messages:
alex.support: FYI incoming from Acme — legal says an API key was exposed in a public staging build. They want: immediate rotation, proof of audit logs for data access, and KMS/HSM key access details for their compliance doc. Can we triage?

maria.incident: ack. do we have the customer request email or a ticket id? need timeline and which key(s) leaked.

samir.cse: ticket #82192 — customer pasted a browser console stacktrace to support. says key inlined in window during onboarding iframe. they pulled logs showing suspicious calls starting 2026-03-16T18:05Z.

kelly.security: high priority. steps we should run now: 1) rotate the exposed API key immediately, 2) collect audit logs (who/when/which endpoints), 3) snapshot KMS/HSM access logs for the last 30 days and hand to legal. can someone confirm access to the customer's CMK ARN?

alex.support: i've created a temporary restricted key for them to continue while we rotate the leaked key. note: customer asked we do rotation on their behalf and provide a signed statement of actions.

samir.cse: repro notes from Acme: onboarding widget includes `window.__REDWOOD_CLIENT_KEY` in dev build. they say it was pushed to staging by their dev, not us. attack vector likely client-side leak, but they want our rotation + audit anyway.

kelly.security: understood. for audit we need these artifacts: - API request logs filtered by suspect key (UTC) - control-plane access logs for KMS CMK usage - HSM access events (if applicable) - any console sign-ins from unusual IPs in the window 2026-02-15..2026-03-16

devon.sre: i'm pulling logs now. quick heads-up on billing: we saw an anomalous token spend spike aligned with the start time. finance flagged it. recommend we create an interim invoice adjustment if misuse confirmed.

samir.cse: customer asked if we can revoke the old key and re-encrypt their stored customer secrets with a new CMK. their infra team uses AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK. they want guidance for rewrapping.

kelly.security: recommended approach (high level): 1) Create a new CMK (or new key version) 2) Grant the same IAM principals 3) Re-encrypt stored ciphertext with the new key (re-wrap) 4) Rotate application config to use new CMK 5) Revoke or disable the leaked API key. We'll provide exact commands.

samir.cse: pinging Acme for their CMK ARN and whether they gave Redwood access to perform rewrap operations. they said legal is ok with us performing actions if we provide audit trail.

kelly.security: commands (AWS CLI examples) to rewrap and disable key — share these with Acme, but require their consent before we run anything that touches their CMK:

```
# create new CMK
aws kms create-key --description "Acme rewrap key 2026-03-16" --tags TagKey=incident,TagValue=82192
# re-encrypt example (S3 object envelope or stored ciphertext)
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ciphertext.bin --source-encryption-context '{"app":"onboard"}' --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/NEW-KEY-ID --output fileb://rewrapped.bin
# disable old key
aws kms disable-key --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/OLD-KEY-ID
```

kelly.security: note: HSM-backed keys may have different constraints; if their CMK is an external HSM provider or CloudHSM, we need their HSM admin to perform the final rewrap step — we can coordinate and provide audit commands.

maria.incident: devon — share the logs slice here. redact any PII. include request_ids and timestamps.

devon.sre: pasted logs: ``SELECT * FROM request_logs WHERE api_key = '[EXPOSED_KEY]' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-16T18:00Z' AND '2026-03-16T20:00Z';`` results: 3,214 requests, endpoints mostly /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings, peak at 18:07Z. attaching truncated CSV to ticket.

alex.support: customer wants an attestation PDF saying: 1) we rotated keys 2) we delivered logs 3) we recommended remediation steps. who can produce the signed attestation?

kelly.security: i will draft the attestation text and sign it with our security lead. need exact timestamps of rotation and the artifacts list. once rotation completes we'll publish SHA256 of the delivered logs bundle for chain-of-custody.

samir.cse: Acme asked if rotating API keys will cause downtime for active sessions. we advised using the temporary key we created, and a canary cutover: config update + 5min warm-up, then revoke old key. they'd accept that.

maria.incident: legal follow-up: they want the KMS/HSM audit log entries to show which principal invoked Encrypt/Decrypt/ReEncrypt and the IP address. can we produce that?

kelly.security: yes — AWS CloudTrail + CloudHSM logs will show principal ARNs and source IPs (if public). if their CMK is customer-managed in their AWS account we will request CloudTrail export from them; if Redwood held the CMK, we can export and sign. need confirmation which account owns the CMK.

devon.sre: action items I'm tracking: - slice API logs and forward to security (in ticket) - block suspicious IPs at LB layer for the next 72h - rate-limit the new temporary key tighter than normal - add anomaly rule to flag repeated high-throughput per-key - give finance the spend slice for chargeback review

deploy-bot: rotation-job created by alex.support for key id [REDACTED], scheduled at 2026-03-16T19:15Z. job id: rj-20260316-41

samir.cse: customer asked for repro steps so they can fix their dev process. suggested guidance we gave: - never embed keys in client JS - use ephemeral session tokens for browser flows - server-side proxy for calls that require secret keys - CORS and cookie-based session protections

kelly.security: final note: we should prepare a short KB article for customers about "If a client-side API key is exposed" — include checklist: rotate, audit, rewrap KMS, reconfigure CI/CD, and legal evidence pack. samir — can you draft?

samir.cse: will draft a KB and link it in the ticket.

maria.incident: we should also escalate to Customer Success for outreach and to ensure Acme gets their compliance pack. cc @csm-acme.

alex.support: thanks team. i'll update ticket #82192 with the attestation template and the rotated key details once rotation completes. keeping this thread for coordination. :white_check_mark:
